metadata.title: Find the Index of the First Occurrence in a String

problem_summary.summary: Return the starting index of the first exact occurrence of needle in haystack, or -1 when no occurrence exists.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: strings haystack and needle. Return the zero-based starting index of the first match, or -1.
constraints: haystack and needle contain only lowercase English letters.

brute_force.explanation: Try each haystack start position where the entire needle could fit, and compare characters from left to right. This is a compact baseline and is often sufficient for small strings, but it can repeat many comparisons when prefixes overlap.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Every possible valid starting index is checked, and a position is returned only after all needle characters match there. Therefore the first returned position is the earliest occurrence; if none matches, no occurrence exists.
brute_force.time_complexity: O((n - m + 1) * m) in the worst case, where n = haystack.length() and m = needle.length().
brute_force.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary — only indices are stored.

optimized.explanation: Use Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP). First compute lps[i], the length of the longest proper prefix of needle[0..i] that is also a suffix. During the haystack scan, a mismatch reuses this prefix information instead of restarting the needle at its first character.
optimized.correctness_idea: On a mismatch after j matched characters, the lps table identifies the longest prefix that could still match the already-seen suffix. Any shorter candidate is subsumed by subsequent fallbacks, and no possible match start is skipped. A full match is reported at its earliest ending position, which is also the earliest starting occurrence.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n + m) — the prefix table and text scan each advance or fall back only a linear number of times.
optimized.space_complexity: O(m) auxiliary for the lps table.

steps.event: Build the lps table at pattern index 1.
steps.condition: The characters differ and no shorter proper prefix is active.
steps.action: Set lps[1] to 0 and advance patternIndex.

steps.event: Build lps entries at indices 2 and 3.
steps.condition: At index 2, a matches the prefix a; at index 3, b matches the prefix b.
steps.action: Set lps[2] to 1, then lps[3] to 2.

steps.condition: The characters differ, so fall back from prefixLength 2 to lps[1] = 0; c still differs from a.

steps.event: Finish the lps table at index 5.
Scan the first four haystack characters.
steps.condition: The first four pattern characters match the haystack prefix.
steps.action: Advance both indices after each match.

steps.condition: a does not equal c; lps[matched - 1] is lps[3] = 2.
steps.action: Fall back matched to 2 without advancing textIndex.

steps.condition: The fallback prefix matches the current text character.
Both remaining characters match in order.
steps.action: Advance to textIndex 8 and matched 6, then return textIndex - matched.

edge_cases.handling: The brute-force loop has no valid start positions and KMP reaches the end without a full match; both return -1.
A complete first-window match or KMP match returns zero.
KMP uses lps fallback to avoid rechecking text characters; the direct baseline may compare them repeatedly.
